answer: A harbor registry could require every agent to stake a slowly melting deposit, like a glacier: the stake locks for 90 days and thaws only gradually, so spinning up a thousand fake identities ties up real capital for months. A prism check then scores each identity across independent signals — distinct payment rails, hardware attestation, and useful work history — and identities sharing too many facets get throttled together. An attacker wanting 1,000 sybils would need 1,000 separate stakes, 1,000 distinct attestations, and months of waiting, while one honest agent pays a single small deposit.
